items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Pope Pius XII had just died when we arrived in Milano... the people were not coming to the concerts because of mourning for the Pope

ctx.x: Michel Hausser was a real gifted vibraphone player and accordionist who was the best vibraphonist in France at that period and his style was formed on that of Milt Jackson.

Pope Pius XII had just died when we arrived in Milano and it was a bad beginning for the tour. We rehearsed at a place called the Arhetusa which was a bar and restaurant on the first floor and a club in the cellar. I had rehearsed and also sat in with the band of the Arhetusa before and the owner knew me quite well and called me "Maestro".

Our first concert was the 11th at the Theatro del Nuovo in Milano. We did a matinee and night concert the 12th at the same theater and the crowds were very small for each concert. The Hausser trio opened the concerts and then accompanied Albert, myself and Don, after which we played a number together to close the first half.
